_what: Which door address and methods each sign-in scope reaches (src/account/sign_in.rs `contract().reach`, checked by src/account/sign_in_check.rs `permits`; `*` is any characters). `scopes` is each scope's own reach. `full_key` is the account's own full key: a sign-in that holds every scope in `holds` (the records and tools an AI app is offered over OAuth, and a browser session of the person's own page) also reaches `reach`, so an AI holding the account's own key can do everything the person's own page can, and is never refused only because it is not the person. Of that reach, `needs_person` names the operations that prove the person is physically present (registering or removing a passkey and its ceremony), each with why; the full key does not reach those, and only a key that holds the `sign-in` scope itself does. A key granted less (one scope, one label, one tool) holds less than `holds` and gets only its own scopes' reach. A guarded change the door makes (src/account/sign_in/known.rs) still asks the known passkey's confirmation of whoever calls it.

needs_person.why: it opens a link that registers a new passkey: registering a passkey proves the person is present
it lists the passkey registrations a passkey link opened: part of registering a passkey
it withdraws a passkey registration a passkey link opened: part of registering a passkey
removing a passkey proves the person is present
a known passkey vouching for another is the person's passkey ceremony
starting or cancelling a passkey recovery replaces which passkeys are known: removing a passkey
it is the passkey ceremony that confirms a guarded change: the person's own presence
applying a grant is the person's act: a passkey confirms the offer it applies
removing a grant is the person's act: a passkey confirms the removal
minting a key is the person's act: a key that carries the sign-in scope needs the person's passkey, and any other key is minted only with scopes its minter holds
